s10.old: The old nickname-first logic miscalled 33 of 536 members. congress.gov uses the OFFICIAL bioguide name = the CSV's `full_name` column, NOT the CSV `nickname` (bioguide says "James P. McGovern" though nickname is "Jim"; a "Jim McGovern" sponsor search returns nothing). It cuts both ways: some official names ARE nicknames (Chuck Edwards, Nikki Budzinski, Gabe Vasquez, Nick LaLota, Val Hoyle, Greg Casar). Rule now: first non-initial given-name token of `full_name` (after stripping "quoted"/(paren) nicknames, initials, suffixes, surname tokens) + `last_name` column. Other corrections: Bernie -> Bernard Sanders, Chuck -> Charles Schumer, Bobby -> Robert Scott, Buddy -> Earl Carter, Rick -> Eric Crawford, Hal -> Harold Rogers, Hank -> Henry Johnson, Chuy -> Jesús García, Mónica -> Monica De La Cruz. The `MEMBER_NAME_OVERRIDES` named vector (defined above the function) is the manual escape hatch for future mismatches; duplicates across members now emit a warning (currently zero collisions). Verified offline against the cached CSV: 536 unique names, all spot names correct, override hook works.

s10.old: - **Optimization round (2026-06-18):** parse re-measured at ~30ms/page on typical pages (62ms was the one giant member's heavier pages) -> real run ~30min @6 cores. Stripping `<script>/<style>/<svg>` before `read_html` measured ZERO speedup (cost is core libxml2 parse, not inline JS) - ruled out, do not retry it. Six wins applied and integration-tested: (1) **shards balanced by URL count** (greedy: heaviest member -> lightest shard, via orchestrator-written `collector_plan.rds`) instead of name-hash, so no shard becomes the tail; (2) **one persistent curl pool per worker** (was per-chunk) -> HTTP/2 keepalive survives across chunks (later changed, see 2026-06-19 crash fix); (3) **retry only transient** (libcurl `fail` + HTTP 5xx); 4xx and empty-200 (JS-only) are permanent `miss`, no wasted second pass - big win on Wayback/dead-URL members; (4) orchestrator builds ONE plan (single index+cache scan) and workers read their slice -> no 6x redundant full scans, lighter workers; (5) heartbeat reads cheap cumulative "ok N" from shard logs (not re-reading all fulltext rds every 30s) + **stall guard** (break if no progress 10min -> survives a crashed worker); (6) `TOTAL_CON` 24 -> 40 (Little's law: ~0.8s latency x ~40/s core needs ~32 in-flight to not starve parse). Plan auto-unlinked at end.
s10.why: "(later changed, see 2026-06-19 crash fix)" is ### Fast pipeline = collector + scraper; collector crash fixed (2026-06-19), later in the same part -press-collector-pipeline

s10.old: - **Graded scale (Haselmayer & Jenny 2017 + Rice & Zorn 2018):** `TONE_LEXICON` data frame carries per-stem intensity weights (1 weak / 2 mid / 3 strong) mirroring GEN_PRO_RX/GEN_ANTI_RX stems. `weighted_tone()` scans CU sentences applying valence shifters; predecessor tokens are derived from the prefix string (not a separate tokenization) so leading/double spaces cannot misalign them. NEGATORS_RX drops the word if it sits in EITHER of the two preceding tokens (2-token reach catches refusal frames "refuses to support"/"failed to protect" that a 1-token window scored as praise); AMPLIFIERS_RX x1.25 (`AMPLIFY_FACTOR`) and DOWNTONERS_RX x0.75 act on the immediate token only. Specific phrases + bill stances enter at weight 3. `graded_from_signed()` adds `+ 0` to collapse IEEE -0.0 -> +0.0. `graded_from_signed(Wp-Wn)` buckets |signed| by `GRADED_CUTS=c(1,2,3.5,5.5,8)` into 0/.2/.4/.6/.8/1.0 (rounded 1 dp).
s10.why: "the two preceding tokens" are text tokens, not a place in the note

s10.old: The "Full text retrieved for 10072 of 12219" gap was NOT random - failures concentrated in the `pagenum` scheme (2107/4521 = 47%; 15 SENATORS at 100%, incl. Senate Banking members Van Hollen/Reed/Collins/Ernst/Cruz...). Root cause: `extract_release` did `suppressWarnings(as.Date(substr(html_attr(t1,"datetime"),1,10)))` - but `as.Date()` THROWS (does not warn) on a non-ISO string, and the IQ-CMS senate.gov sites put a non-ISO value in `<time datetime>`. `suppressWarnings` does not catch errors -> `extract_release` aborted for the WHOLE page -> empty body -> counted as failed fetch. FIX: `attr_date()` helper wraps `as.Date` in tryCatch then falls back to `parse_release_date`; used for both `<time datetime>` and the meta-date tags. Validated live on ernst.senate.gov: now returns date 2026-06-05 + 2688-char body (was NA). SELF-HEALING: `fetch_member_fulltext`'s `done` set requires body AND date, so these empty-body releases are already in `todo` and auto-refetch on the next live run (no force needed). NOTE: these IQ-CMS pages lack article/main/.entry-content selectors so body falls back to whole-page `<body>` (incl. nav chrome) - works for scoring but a dedicated IQ-CMS body selector would be cleaner (follow-up). Also: 458 members at Stage 4 is NOT a bug - it is the topical funnel (537 roster -> 532 with indexed releases -> 458 with >=1 finance/CU-titled release); the 74 dropped are mostly local non-CU press, though a few finance senators (Crapo/Cornyn/Grassley) have poor index extraction yielding only nav labels.

Only use `VAR=x prog` syntax when put in Git Bash. Also: scripts that reference sibling files by relative name must run from the project dir - `run_cu_pipeline.R` now self-locates (setwd to its own `--file=` dir) so launch cwd no longer matters; the bare scraper/collector still expect the project dir as cwd (the collector later also self-locates, 2026-06-21).
